rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should explore a promising multimodal configuration. This experiment tests a multimodal model with scvi_n200 (RNA) and resnet50 (image) encoders, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion—standard components that balance complexity and performance. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines, which is critical for guiding subsequent experiments.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, resnet50, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves 0.6776 accuracy. This experiment tests changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method the same. This clarifies whether transformer aggregation improves performance on the same encoder setup, balancing exploitation of the base configuration with exploration of a key architectural change.

The existing evidence shows config_022 (multimodal, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'weighted' to 'concat' while retaining 'transformer' aggregation (a key component of config_022) could improve performance. It clarifies the importance of fusion strategy in multimodal settings, balancing exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of design choices. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly addresses a critical hyperparameter with minimal deviation from the proven-effective configuration.

The existing evidence shows config_022 (multimodal, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while keeping the high-performing transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. This clarifies whether upgrading the image encoder could further improve performance, balancing exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of a key component difference.

Existing evidence shows config_041 (imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation + weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from transformer to avgpool (while keeping other parameters identical) could improve or confirm the current best. It clarifies the impact of aggregation method on performance, balancing exploitation of the top-performing image encoder with exploration of alternative aggregation strategies.

The existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder with scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_041) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests avgpool aggregation and concat fusion with the same RNA and image encoders, clarifying whether the current best's transformer aggregation and weighted fusion are optimal. It balances exploitation (testing similar components) and exploration (varying aggregation/fusion) to reduce uncertainty about critical design choices.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_041) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, clarifying whether RNA encoder choice or fusion method has greater impact. It balances exploration of RNA encoder variations while maintaining high-performing aggregation and image encoder settings.

The existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_041) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.725). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt while keeping the high-performing image encoder, aggregation, and fusion settings. This clarifies whether scgpt, a more advanced RNA encoder, could further improve accuracy, leveraging the strong foundation of the current top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows config_041 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) has the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing fusion from weighted to concat while keeping transformer aggregation (a strong performer) affects accuracy. It clarifies if fusion method is critical, balancing exploitation of current best parameters with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows config_041 (0.725 accuracy) is the top performer using scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, but with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_044), which could clarify if changing aggregation/fusion methods improves accuracy. Since this is the final experiment, testing a variant of the top-performing configuration (same RNA/image encoders) is the best use of the budget to potentially break ties or confirm robustness.
